initial.name: aether_call
initial.description: Call one native AetherShell builtin with positional JSON arguments and return its typed result. `builtin` is one flat native name (`ls`, `crypto_hash`, `json_parse`); find names with `aether_discover`. Arguments travel on the interpreter's typed argument channel, which this call verified, so a string containing `${` and a non-identifier object key are data rather than source. A process-capable builtin runs under this call's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than reads, network, or process control; the interpreter's own `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. Foreground only, under a hard deadline. A result larger than the deployment's budgets fails loudly and names the narrowing remedy instead of returning a partial value. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this call: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

builtin.description: Flat native builtin name, for example "ls" or "crypto_hash".

args.description: Positional arguments in the order the builtin's signature declares them; JSON data only.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin kills the interpreter. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_discover
initial.description: Read the native AetherShell ontology. Without `query`, return one page of the category manifest with each category's builtin count and effect classes. With a category name, return one page of that category's builtins with their signatures and effects. With a builtin name, return its parameters, return type, effects, aliases, and examples. A name the ontology does not know returns the interpreter's own unknown-name reply, which is a successful result rather than a failure. Page a list with `offset` and `limit`; a page that leaves entries behind reports `nextOffset`. Foreground only, under a hard deadline.

query.description: Ontology category or builtin name to describe (for example "Crypto" or "crypto_hash"). Omit for the category manifest.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first entry to return (default 0). Continue a list with the previous page's nextOffset.

limit.description: Maximum entries in this page; the deployment's ontology-entry budget caps it.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin kills the interpreter. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_eval
initial.description: Evaluate one AetherShell program and return its canonical JSON value. Unlike the other tools, the program runs on the interpreter's own command line, so lambdas, modules such as `file.read("notes.txt")`, and multi-statement programs work and are not limited to flat builtin names. The program must exit successfully for a value; a failing program returns the interpreter's own error text. A program that prints nothing reports `resultType: "none"`. Everything the program does runs under this call's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control. The interpreter's `sh` switch starts off, but that is a convenience default rather than a boundary, because the program can change its own environment and reach the process builtins either way. Numbers outside the exact integer range this runtime can carry are rejected rather than rounded, so ask for such a value as text. Foreground only, under a hard deadline. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this call: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

code.description: AetherShell program text: an expression, a lambda, or a sequence of statements.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin kills the interpreter. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_job_start
initial.description: Start one AetherShell program as a background job and return its job id immediately. This is the streaming counterpart of `aether_eval`: the program runs on the interpreter's own command line, but no result document is read, so a program that prints logs, mixed JSON, or nothing at all still completes. Read the interpreter's raw stdout and stderr with `job_output`; the canonical exit facts and any spill file arrive with the first read after settlement. `job_kill` requests a stop; settlement follows managed-process cleanup. Each job is a fresh interpreter process: no variables, functions, or directory changes persist. The job runs without a deadline unless this deployment caps job runtime or the call supplies `timeoutMs`. The job belongs to this session and is stopped when this session's agent is disposed or the plugin unloads. Output a program's own children produce through the interpreter's process builtins may be captured by the interpreter until it returns it, so realtime child logs are not promised. The job uses this session's DSH file policy as it stood when the job started, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control; the interpreter's `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this job: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

code.description: AetherShell program text to run in the background: an expression, a lambda, or a sequence of statements.

label.description: Short human-facing label for this job, shown in job listings and the UI. Omit to use the program's first line.

cwd.description: Working directory for this job. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds for the whole job. Omitted, the job runs until it finishes or `job_kill` stops it, bounded only by this deployment's job-runtime cap when one is set.

initial.name: aether_pipeline
initial.description: Run an ordered native AetherShell pipeline, each step calling one flat builtin and feeding its result to the next. `select` maps each item of that step's result through a dotted field path, so `select: "name"` reads the `name` field of every element. `predicate` is an AetherShell expression passed to that step's builtin as its lambda first argument and replaces the step's `args`. `input` starts the pipeline from a value instead of from the first call. Step arguments travel on the same verified typed channel as `aether_call`, and every step runs under this call's DSH file policy. Foreground only, under a hard deadline. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this call: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

steps.description: Steps in execution order; at least one is required.

builtin.description: Flat native builtin name this step calls.

args.description: Positional arguments for this step; JSON data only.

select.description: Dotted field path read from each element of this step's result, for example "name" or "meta.size".

predicate.description: AetherShell expression passed to this step's builtin as `fn(x) => <predicate>`; replaces this step's args.

input.description: Value that starts the pipeline; omit it to start from the first step's call. An explicit null is sent as the None value, which this deployment verified the interpreter delivers.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin kills the interpreter. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_close
initial.description: Close one of this agent's persistent AetherShell sessions and terminate its interpreter process. The native session is asked to close first, and the process is terminated afterwards whatever the interpreter answered, so a closed session never keeps running. Closing needs no new policy grant and always releases the process. Closing an id this agent does not hold reports `closed: false` and changes nothing; another agent's session is refused.

session_id.description: Opaque session id returned by aether_session_open.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_eval
initial.description: Evaluate one AetherShell program inside a persistent session and return its typed value. Unlike `aether_eval`, the program runs in the session's own long-lived process, so variables, functions, the current directory, and the environment all persist between calls and modules such as `file.read("notes.txt")` are available. A session is one real interpreter process on this host, holding native mutable state (variables, functions, the current directory, and the process environment) that survives between calls. That separation is the interpreter's own: two sessions do not share variables, functions, or a working directory, but they share the host itself, so files, network access, and every external service are common to all of them and to this machine. The plugin does not checkpoint interpreter state and does not replay commands, so nothing survives reopening a session and a session does not outlive the plugin or the harness process; the programs you send still read and write real host files. The code you send really runs, with real effects on this host. Its file writes and deletes run under the calling session's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control; the interpreter's own `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. The interpreter's evaluation surface is broad and is not restricted to builtin names. A failing program does not roll back what earlier statements in the same call already did. Requests carry a host-random nonce, so output the program prints is returned as bounded `logs` rather than mistaken for a result. One evaluation runs at a time per session. A call that reaches its deadline or is cancelled terminates the whole session process, because the interpreter cannot abandon a running command; open a new session to continue. An access the DSH file policy denies is final: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

session_id.description: Opaque session id returned by aether_session_open.

code.description: AetherShell program text: an expression, a lambda, or a sequence of statements executed in the session.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_list
initial.description: List the persistent AetherShell sessions this agent currently holds, with each one's opaque id, label, working directory, state, and file-policy mode. Sessions the calling session's DSH file policy no longer matches are closed here and reported as destroyed rather than shown as usable. Pass `usage: true` to add the interpreter's own evaluation and token counters for each live session, which costs one request per session. Another agent's sessions are never listed. An access the DSH file policy denies is final: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

usage.description: Also read each live session's counters from the interpreter (one request per session).

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_open
initial.description: Open a persistent AetherShell session and return an opaque session id. A session is one real interpreter process on this host, holding native mutable state (variables, functions, the current directory, and the process environment) that survives between calls. That separation is the interpreter's own: two sessions do not share variables, functions, or a working directory, but they share the host itself, so files, network access, and every external service are common to all of them and to this machine. The plugin does not checkpoint interpreter state and does not replay commands, so nothing survives reopening a session and a session does not outlive the plugin or the harness process; the programs you send still read and write real host files. The code you send really runs, with real effects on this host. Its file writes and deletes run under the calling session's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control; the interpreter's own `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. The interpreter's evaluation surface is broad and is not restricted to builtin names. Use `aether_session_eval` to run programs in it. Sessions are private to the agent that opened them, the deployment caps how many one agent may hold, and an idle session is closed automatically. The returned handle carries the DSH file policy it was opened under; if that policy later changes the session is closed rather than reused. An access the DSH file policy denies is final: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

cwd.description: Working directory for the interpreter process. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

name.description: Optional label echoed by aether_session_list so you can tell sessions apart.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_read
initial.description: Drain the output a persistent AetherShell session has written since the last drain, without running a program. A session may host a child or a service that keeps writing while no call is in flight, and every `aether_session_eval` already returns the output it saw; this tool reads whatever is left. Output is delivered exactly once: a second read with nothing new reports an empty result. Reading a session that has a call in flight is refused, because that output belongs to the call. Reading a closed or unknown session reports that the id is not open. Bounded like every other log, with the complete stream path when the retained tail was cut.

session_id.description: Opaque session id returned by aether_session_open.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: edit
initial.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

initial.name: exit_plan_mode
initial.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

initial.name: get_goal
initial.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Set path to the narrowest known directory; a directory prefix in pattern does not narrow the search root. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to filter file paths (e.g. "**/*.ts", "**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth. A directory prefix filters matches but does not narrow the search root; set path to the directory to search.

path.description: Directory tree to search; use the narrowest known directory. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now; inactive means no turn is executing, whether the child is loaded or must be resumed. inactive does not describe task completion, success, failure, or waiting for other agents. A `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts or resumes a turn for an inactive child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics only in `descendants` scope. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

initial.name: read
initial.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

initial.name: read_image
initial.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is inactive, the message starts or resumes a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

initial.name: skill
initial.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts or resumes a turn while it is inactive. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

initial.name: subagent_fork
initial.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the subagent and returns its result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

initial.name: todo_write
initial.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

initial.name: update_goal
initial.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

initial.name: web_fetch
initial.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

initial.name: web_search
initial.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground by default: this call returns when the whole script finishes. Set `run_in_background: true` for a long run: the call returns a job id immediately, the run keeps orchestrating in the background, and its return value arrives with the job's completion notice (check on it with `job_output`, stop it with `job_kill`).

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

initial.name: write
initial.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.
